The UI could be better:

The core problem is that the agent built a stack of sections and treated the toggles as “show more”, not as a navigation model. Most of the other issues follow from that. Here is what I see in the three screenshots, grouped by area.

1. Navigation and page structure (the biggest issue)

What’s wrong

Settings opens above Reports and pushes everything down. Two “pages” end up on screen at once, and you have to scroll past Settings to reach the thing you were using.
The header mixes four kinds of control in one row of identical buttons: views (Cases, Reports), a primary action (New complaint), configuration (Settings) and a utility (Refresh).
The active state is unclear. “Reports” has a blue outline, while “New complaint” is solid blue, so it looks like the selected one.
“Close” on the Settings panel is the only way back, so it behaves like a dropdown, not a destination.

Fix

Use exactly one active view at a time, held in state and reflected in the URL (#/cases, #/reports, #/settings) so the Back button and refresh work.
Split the header by role:
Tabs (Atlassian Tabs pattern) for Cases and Reports, with a clear underline on the active one.
One primary button on the right: Create complaint.
Icon buttons for Settings (gear) and Refresh. Better still, drop Refresh and show “Updated 2 min ago” with auto-refresh.
New complaint should open as a modal or a right-hand drawer over the current view, not as another stacked section.
Settings should be either a small popover or modal for two preferences, or a proper view. It shouldn’t be an inline panel.
2. Settings

What’s wrong

“Publication status” is a sync log with 11 lines of “Changes saved. Sheet update is pending.” and 11 “View complaint” buttons. It’s system plumbing sitting in the user’s preference panel.
“Sheet update”, “publication” and “pending” are internal jargon. A staff member doesn’t know what a sheet update is, or whether they need to do anything.
It’s not clear whether the preferences apply per user or per device (“on your devices”), and there’s no confirmation after Save.
Default queue and Default branch are full-width selects for a two-option choice.

Fix

Collapse the sync status into one summary indicator (an Atlassian inline message or banner): “11 changes waiting to sync to Google Sheets”, with a “Details” link. Only per-item rows that failed need a Retry action.
Move the status out of Settings entirely, into a small status chip in the header or an admin-only view.
Constrain form width to about 400 to 480px, and show a success flag (“Preferences saved”) after saving.
3. Cases view

What’s wrong

“Update complaint” is a dropdown defaulting to “Resolve complaint”. The final action is pre-selected, and the form is always open. This invites accidental resolutions. The Cancel button also cancels nothing, since nothing is in progress.
The form takes the most important space. The complaint’s history (Activity) is buried at the bottom below an empty “Photos and documents” section. People need to read context before acting.
“Photos and documents” appears twice: once as upload buttons inside the form and once as an empty “No documents available” section below.
“Not resolved” is repeated on every row, plus in the detail header, plus in the filter. Three repeats add no information.
The row design is clumsy. The name sits in a button-like chip, and the status is plain text. Status isn’t scannable.
The Search button is detached from the inputs and not aligned with them.
National ID is shown in full, which is a privacy concern. Mask it (•••••••99) with a reveal action.
No visible keyboard or mobile behavior: a 1/3 + 2/3 split will break on a phone. Since this is a ported mini app, mobile matters most.

Fix

Detail layout, top to bottom: header (name, reference, status lozenge) → key details → description → Activity timeline → Attachments → action bar.
Replace the dropdown with an action bar: Add note, Resolve, Reopen (only valid actions for the current status). Clicking Resolve opens a small modal with the required note and attachments, and Cancel makes sense there.
Use Lozenges for status, not text: Open (blue), Reopened (orange), Closed (green).
Make search live (debounced) and drop the Search button, or place it inside the field.
On mobile, show list → tap → detail with a Back arrow.
4. Reports view

What’s wrong

Eight filter controls are visible at once, and the default Period is “Custom dates” with two empty mm/dd/yyyy fields. The default state of a report shouldn’t be “you must pick dates”.
Jargon in the filters: “Dates apply to / Reported complaints”, “View by”. These are hard to parse without reading the helper line.
Date formats are inconsistent. Inputs use mm/dd/yyyy, while the charts use 01-09-26. That reads as 1 September or 9 January, depending on who looks. It’s also labeled by day even though the grouping is by month.
The charts add little. “Complaint types” is a bar chart with one bar. “Status of reported complaints” is two bars over two dates and duplicates the KPI cards. The gap between the two data points makes both bar charts look empty, and it wastes most of the width.
Drill-down by dropdown. “Select cases in reported vs resolved” is an empty, unlabeled select. Nobody will guess that it lists cases, because drill-down should happen by clicking a bar.
A chart-type dropdown on every chart is clutter. Nobody needs to switch bar to line on a chart with two points.
Terminology drifts: Not resolved / Open / Reopened / Resolved / Closed all appear across the page. Pick one set.
The “table” isn’t a table. It’s a list with no columns, no sorting, no dates, and the pager says “Page 1 · 11 complaints” with both buttons disabled.
KPI cards are passive: no comparison to the previous period, and not clickable to filter.
The three export buttons (Download Excel, Email report, Email settings) have equal weight. Email settings is configuration, not an action on this report.
The layout leaves a dead gap beside Reported vs resolved, because the two cards have different heights.

Fix

Default to a preset, such as Last 30 days, with a compact filter bar. Show From/To only if “Custom” is chosen, and put Branch and Type under a “More filters” control.
Use plain labels: “Date range”, “Group by”, and one tooltip on “Count by: reported date / resolved date”.
Use one date format everywhere, such as 22 Oct 2026 (this also avoids the dd/mm vs mm/dd confusion). Month grouping should label ticks “Sep 2026”.
Make the KPI cards clickable (Total, Open, Resolved) and show a delta (“+3 vs last period”).
Merge or replace the charts:
One trend chart: reported vs resolved over time, as a line or bar.
One breakdown that appears only when there’s more than one category.
Clicking any bar or point opens a drawer listing those cases.
Use a proper Dynamic table with columns: Reference, Customer, Branch, Type, Reported, Age, Status (lozenge). Sorting, row click opens the case, and drop pagination under about 25 rows.
Group the buttons: Export as a single split button (Excel / Email), with scheduling in Settings.
5. Cross-cutting issues
Spacing and hierarchy: the “Complaints” H1 and “Reports” H2 sit almost touching, with the action buttons crammed beside the H2. Atlassian’s 8px grid and page-header pattern (title, then breadcrumb or tabs, then actions on the right) would fix this.
One primary action per view. Right now, blue appears on Reports, New complaint, Save preferences and Resolve complaint. That’s the primary color used for everything.
Color alone carries meaning (green/red bars). Add labels or patterns for accessibility, and consider whether red for “Open” implies a failure when it’s normal work in progress.
Missing states: no loading skeletons, empty states, error messages or success flags visible anywhere.
Sample data hides problems. Everything is “System service” at “Synthetic Other Branch”, so the filters and charts can’t show whether they work. Seed varied data before judging the design.
A prompt you can give the agent

Restructure the Complaints page as a single-page app with exactly one active view at a time: Cases, Reports, Settings. Use hash routing so Back and refresh work. Header: tabs for Cases and Reports on the left; one primary “Create complaint” button, a gear icon for Settings, and “Updated X min ago” instead of a Refresh button on the right. Never append a view below another. “Create complaint” opens in a modal or right-side drawer. Follow Atlassian Design System components: Tabs, Page header, Lozenge for status (Open blue, Reopened orange, Closed green), Dynamic table with sortable columns, Inline message for sync status, Modal for confirmations, Flags for success messages. Cases detail: header with status lozenge, details, description, Activity timeline, Attachments, then an action bar with Add note / Resolve / Reopen. Resolve opens a modal with the required note and attachments. Reports: default to Last 30 days, hide From/To unless Custom, one trend chart and one breakdown, clickable KPI cards, a real table below, a single Export menu. Move the “publication status” out of Settings into a one-line sync indicator with a details link. Use the date format 22 Oct 2026 everywhere. Use one status vocabulary: Open, Reopened, Closed. Design mobile first: list → detail with a Back arrow.

If it would help, I can sketch a wireframe of the new Cases and Reports layouts so the agent has a visual target, since agents tend to follow a picture better than a description.

there other issues, does the fields have to be that long, symmetry issues, organisation etc dig deeper , criticize more, overlook nothing

You’re right to push on this. Here is a second pass that goes past the navigation problem into sizing, symmetry, grouping, hierarchy, charts, copy and consistency.

1. Field and control sizing
Every input is full-width on a ~1,900px canvas. The Settings selects, the Report picker, the “Update complaint” select, the Resolution note and the chart-type selects all stretch 1,000-1,700px to hold values like “Not resolved” or “Bar”. Long fields make scanning slow, hide how much input is expected, and look broken on wide monitors.
Fix: size fields to their content. Use Atlassian’s width scale: small ≈160px for status and type selects, medium ≈200px, large ≈320px, xlarge ≈480px for the search and the note. Cap a form at about 480px and the page content at about 1,200-1,440px, centered.
Selects used for 2-3 options. “Chart type: Bar”, Default queue and “Update complaint” don’t need dropdowns.
Fix: use a segmented control or toggle for chart type, radio buttons for the default queue, and an action bar instead of “Update complaint”.
The Search button is shorter than the inputs and sits detached at the far right. It is not vertically aligned with the fields, so the row reads as ragged.
Fix: use the same 40px control height everywhere, put the magnifier inside the field, and drop the button if search is live.
The “Select cases in …” dropdowns are different widths in each card (about 340px in Complaint types, 50% in Reported vs resolved, 50% of full width in Status). The controls under each chart follow no rule.
Date inputs show mm/dd/yyyy for staff in Kenya, where dd/mm/yyyy is the norm. The charts use 01-09-26, which is a third format.
2. Grid, alignment and symmetry
The sections sit on different grids. Filters use 4 columns, KPI cards use 3, and charts use 2. Edges don’t line up from one band to the next (the second KPI card starts at ~592px, but no filter column does).
Fix: use one 12-column grid. Filters in groups of 3 or 4, KPIs in 4 (Total, Open, Reopened, Closed), charts 8/4 or 6/6.
The KPI cards are ~550px wide for a single digit. The number is left-aligned, so each card is two-thirds empty.
Fix: make them compact (~200-240px), and add a delta or sparkline so there is something worth the space.
The chart row is unbalanced. Reported vs resolved is taller than Complaint types because it carries two extra controls, which leaves a dead block under the right card. Then the next chart is full width at ~170px plot height and ~1,600px wide, so it is a thin strip with two bars at the extremes.
The Cases split gives the list about 740px, but each row fills only about half of it. The detail pane then has two 550px columns holding values like CMP-7. Both panes are mostly whitespace while content is jammed into small text.
Fix: list ≈ 360-420px, detail takes the rest, with detail content capped at ~720px.
Two rows of right-aligned buttons stack at the top of Reports (the view/action buttons, then Download / Email / Email settings), pressed against each other and the H1. That is two competing toolbars in 60px.
Spacing rhythm is inconsistent. The H1 to H2 gap is tiny, the filter rows are packed tighter than the card padding, and the gaps between bands vary. Pick the 8px scale (8/16/24/32) and use it by rule: 16px inside groups, 24px between groups, 32px between sections.
3. Information organization
Filters are grouped by where the grid happened to wrap, not by meaning.
Period sits at the end of row 2, but its From/To are at the start of row 3. A dependent field is separated from its parent.
Date concepts (Dates apply to, Period, From, To) are interleaved with “View by”, which is a display setting, and with Branch and Type, which are scope filters.
Fix: three clusters.
Date: Date range, Count by reported/resolved date, with From/To appearing only for Custom.
Scope: Status, Branch, Type.
Display: Group by.
Put the Report picker in tabs or a segmented control, not a full-width select.
The filters don’t apply to everything. The page says dates apply to the totals and table, but each chart “explains its own dates”. A filter bar that only governs some of the page breaks the user’s mental model. If I narrow to last week, I expect every number on screen to change.
“Period: Custom dates” with empty From/To is a contradictory default. The page shows 11 complaints, so empty must mean all time, but nothing says so. Default to a real preset and show the resolved range (“1 Sep - 22 Oct 2026”).
There is no filter feedback. No “Reset”, no active-filter count, no indication of whether changes apply instantly or need a button. Reports applies live while Cases has a Search button, so there are two interaction models in one app.
The Cases detail ordering is wrong. The description has no heading, no weight, and sits between the metadata and the form, so it reads as a stray line. It is the most important content. Detail fields are laid out in a two-column zigzag (Reference/ID, Phone/Branch, Type/Reported) with no grouping.
Fix: Customer (name, ID masked, phone) and Complaint (reference, type, branch, reported, age) as two groups. The description comes next under a “Description” heading.
The Publication status list is in random order (1, 11, 9, 10, 2, 3, 4, 8, 5, 6, 7), and the complaints table is in the same unexplained order. Users can’t tell what the sort is. Default to newest first or oldest unresolved first, and show a sort indicator.
4. Visual hierarchy and typography
The scale is flat. The H1 is ~20px, section titles ~15px bold, field labels ~11px bold, helper text ~11px gray. The text that carries the data (customer names, metadata, helper copy) is small for a desktop view. Atlassian body text is 14px, so there is a lot of room to increase.
Field labels are as heavy as headings but a third of the size. That inverts hierarchy. Labels should be 12px semibold in a subtle color and headings should be clearly larger.
Status is plain, small, gray text (OPEN, CLOSED, Not resolved), placed 1,000+px from the name. The most scannable attribute on the page has no visual weight.
There are no container rules. Settings is a card, the Reports header is not, the filters float without a container, the KPIs and charts are cards, the table is a card. Pick one: a filter bar container, then cards for content.
The metadata string (CMP-7 · Synthetic Other Branch · System service · Open for 35 days) packs four facts into one small gray line. Reference, branch, type and age cannot be scanned or sorted.
5. Charts
The x-axis is a time scale with only two points. That puts bars at the far-left and far-right edges with 1,500px of nothing between them.
Fix: use a categorical axis for monthly buckets (Sep 2026, Oct 2026), so the bars sit together and have a sensible width.
Zero-value bars still carry labels (0), and every bar has a data label on top of the y-axis, so numbers are shown twice. Keep either labels or axis ticks, and drop zero labels.
Legends sit below the chart, away from the data, then two controls below that. Three layers of chrome per chart. Put the legend above the plot, inline with the title.
The same color means different things. Blue is “Reported” in one chart and “Complaints” in another. Red is “Open/Reopened”, which signals error for what is routine work.
Each chart carries a paragraph of explanation. If a chart needs 30 words to explain what it counts, the title is wrong. Use a precise title and put the rest in an info tooltip.
There are no tooltips or hover states, and the drill-down is a hidden empty dropdown. Clicking a bar should open the cases behind it.
The Complaint types chart has one bar and the Status chart repeats the KPIs. Neither earns its space with this data. Hide breakdowns with a single category, or turn the card into a compact list with counts.
The y-axis is capped at exactly the maximum (10 with a bar of 10), so the label collides with the top edge. Add headroom.
6. Cases (master-detail)
Selection is shown as a border around the name only, not the row. Highlight the whole row with a left accent.
The numbered list (1-7) adds nothing, and “Not resolved” repeats on every row. Replace both with a status lozenge and the age.
Age is the key triage signal and it is buried. “Open for 35 days” should be visually distinct, with an escalation color past a threshold, and the list should show it as a column or right-aligned value.
Pagination on a master-detail list (“Page 1 of 1”) is the wrong pattern. Use a scrolling list with a count.
Attachments appear twice (upload buttons in the form, then an empty “Photos and documents” section below the Cancel button), so the form appears to continue after its own submit buttons.
“Take photo” on desktop is a leftover from the Telegram mini app. Use one “Attach files” control with drag-and-drop, accepted types and a size limit. Offer camera capture only on mobile.
“Resolve complaint” appears twice (the dropdown value and the button), and Cancel cancels nothing because no action has started.
“No activity recorded” on a 35-day-old case looks like a data bug. The creation event (“Reported by …”) should always be the first activity entry.
“Reported (Nairobi)” exposes a timezone implementation detail. Show 17 Sep 2026, 13:28 (35 days ago).
There is no way to copy a link to a case, and no “next case” after resolving, so every resolution ends at the same place and the worker must find the next one.
The National ID is shown in full and in plain text. Mask it by default.
7. Tables and lists

The “table” has no columns, so you can’t sort, compare dates or scan one attribute. It needs headers: Reference, Customer, Branch, Type, Reported, Age, Status. Rows must be fully clickable with a hover state, and pagination should disappear when it has nothing to page (both buttons are disabled, and the footer says “Page 1 · 11 complaints” here but “Page 1 of 1” on Cases).

8. Copy and consistency
There are five words for the same thing: Complaints, Cases, “View complaint”, “7 cases”, “11 complaints”. Pick one.
Four status vocabularies: Not resolved / Open, Resolved / Closed, Open / Reopened, and “Queue” in Settings versus “Status” in Cases. Use Open, Reopened, Closed everywhere, with “Open + Reopened” as the unresolved group.
Internal language leaks into the UI: “Publication status”, “Sheet update is pending”, “reported cohort”, “Dates apply to”, and the field-name-as-sentence “The Dates apply to filter does not change this reporting-date basis.”
Settings helper text under Default branch refers to the queue, so it is unclear which field it belongs to.
9. Shell and global gaps
“JBL Staff workspace” implies a multi-app workspace, but there is no app switcher, no breadcrumb and no indication of who is signed in or at which branch. “Sign out” is a bare text link.
There is no sticky filter bar or header, so on a ~2,000px page the filters disappear before you reach the table.
There are no loading, empty or error states, and no success feedback after saving or resolving.
Seed data is uniform (one branch, one type, two dates), so the filters and charts can’t prove they work. Seed 30-50 varied records across several months and branches before judging.
10. Accessibility and mobile
Gray helper text at ~11px on dark has weak contrast, and chart series are distinguished by color alone. Add patterns or direct labels.
Controls look about 30-34px tall, which is under a comfortable touch target on a phone. Use 40-44px on mobile.
A 4-column filter grid, three KPI cards and a two-pane layout have no visible responsive plan. Since this was a phone mini app, test at 375px first.
Add this to your prompt

Layout rules: one 12-column grid, content max-width 1,280px centered, 8px spacing scale (16 within groups, 24 between groups, 32 between sections). Field widths by content (small 160, medium 200, large 320, xlarge 480), forms max 480px, no full-width selects. Body text 14px, labels 12px semibold subtle, one clear heading scale. Filters: a single sticky filter bar with three clusters (Date, Scope, Display), a Reset action and an active-filter count, applied live and affecting every number on the page. Status: Lozenges only, vocabulary Open / Reopened / Closed, used everywhere. Charts: categorical axes, no zero labels, legend above, tooltips, click-to-drill-down, explanations in info tooltips, hide single-category breakdowns. Table: real columns, sortable, row click, default sort newest first. Cases: compact list (~400px) with age and lozenge, detail in groups (Customer, Complaint), description under its own heading, Activity timeline starting with the creation event, an action bar instead of a dropdown, one “Attach files” control, masked National ID, copyable link, next-case after resolve. Terminology: “Complaints” only, never “cases”.
